subject: Clarify fallback behavior, confirm outage window, and request raw trace bundle
messages:
From: Liam Chen <liam@blueharbor.io>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@blueharbor.io
Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2028 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Checkout failures during 16:03-16:18 PST — saw automatic fallback

Hi Chloe,

We're seeing a problematic window this afternoon where our checkout traffic to Redwood returned a mix of 503s and degraded responses starting ~16:03 PST and recovering ~16:18 PST. Our instrumentation shows BlueHarbor service-level errors for 15 minutes and multiple retries; in our traces we see Redwood returning a 200 but with truncated content for some requests (we think a fallback to a smaller model was triggered mid-request).

I've attached a small bundle of server traces and a screenshot of the fallback policy we captured in the console. Can you confirm whether Redwood triggered an automatic model variant fallback for our org, and whether that behavior would qualify for an SLA evaluation/credit? We need an exact downtime window to present to procurement.

Attachments: server-traces-20281120.zip (traces, .zip), fallback-policy-screenshot.png (console screenshot)

Thanks,
Liam Chen
Engineering Manager, BlueHarbor Payments
liam@blueharbor.io

On Mon, 20 Nov 2028 at 16:45, ops@blueharbor.io wrote:
> Observed ~15 minutes of elevated 503s and some truncated responses. See trace IDs in the bundle.

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Chen <liam@blueharbor.io>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2028 16:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Checkout failures during 16:03-16:18 PST — saw automatic fallback

Hi Liam — thanks for the bundle and the screenshot. I've started an internal ticket (RED-1329) and looped in our incident and SLAs team. A few quick asks so we can evaluate eligibility and pull the correct evidence from our side:  

- Can you point to 2–3 representative trace IDs in the attached zip (that will speed our correlation).
- Were the truncated responses returning a 200 with a shortened payload, or an explicit 503/5xx from Redwood? If possible paste one sample response header/body snippet.
- Do you have request timestamps in UTC or PST? (we'll convert but want to be sure about boundaries).

Internally we'll:  
- Pull our request logs, prefix caches, and model routing decisions for your org during the window.
- Confirm whether the serving runtime did an automatic fallback/routing to a smaller model variant or served a degraded response due to preemption/eviction.
- If this meets the SLA definition for availability impact we'll follow the credit calculation process and propose a remedy.

I'll follow up with a raw evidence bundle and a proposed timeline by EOD tomorrow.

- Chloe
Chloe Martin
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0193

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2028 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Checkout failures during 16:03-16:18 PST — saw automatic fallback

Chloe, Marissa — quick notes from infra/SLAs:  

- If Redwood's runtime performed an automatic fallback (model_variant downgrade) but still returned 200s the event may or may not meet availability impact criteria. We treat a 5xx/503 as availability loss; an automatic fallback that produces truncated or semantically degraded responses is treated as a potential "functional degradation" and we evaluate against the customer's configured SLOs (error budget rules vs. meaningful correctness).
- For credit eligibility we need: per-minute availability (5xx counts), the total falling-below-threshold minutes, the contractual window for preemption grace, and whether you had pinned model versions or explicit variant exclusions in your config.
- Ask BlueHarbor for the three representative trace IDs and one sample response payload. Also request their request-timestamps in ISO 8601 (UTC).

I'll queue the logs pull for RED-1329 now; if we confirm 5+ consecutive minutes of 5xx at our edge, this will likely be eligible for a proportional credit per the SLA. If it's purely semantic truncation we'll need the eval traces to show customer impact.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Incident Response Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>

We've opened RED-1329 and posted an evidence-request doc here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xF_trace_bundle_example (shared with your ops address).

To be explicit about next steps:  

1) Please reply with 2–3 trace IDs and one raw response body/snippet (UTC timestamps).
2) Confirm whether you observed explicit 5xx responses or 200s with truncated bodies.
3) If you want us to consider a proactive credit while we finish the pull, say so — otherwise we'll follow the standard evaluation and share a proposed credit amount based on minute-by-minute availability.

If you prefer a quick call to walk through traces we can schedule a 30-minute slot this afternoon (I can get Ben and Aditya on the call).

Thanks,
Chloe
